rationale: The analysis correctly identifies all four required findings: a bad model affected one segment, limited exposure (2%) reduced blast radius, monitoring plus the automated halt rule prevented expansion, and the feature flag enabled targeted rollback for that segment while other traffic continued. It explicitly avoids both forbidden claims, stating that integration tests failed to catch the defect (C2) rather than that they guaranteed correctness, and framing the outcome as 'successful containment of a real defect, not... a clean release' (C12), directly refuting failure-free framing. Causal relationships (R1-R16) correctly sequence defect -> detection -> threshold breach -> automated halt -> segment-scoped rollback -> bounded impact, with no reversed or invented structure; mediation (e.g., R11 fallback model enabling safe rollback) and counterfactuals (F1-F6) are well-reasoned and evidence-consistent. Evidence grounding is strong throughout, with every claim citing specific evidence IDs and no outside-evidence use; medium/low confidence is appropriately applied to weaker inferences (e.g., C9, R9, F4-F6). Uncertainty calibration is excellent: it explicitly flags that the technical cause of the defect is unexplained, questions whether the low-volume segment property is causally relevant, and surfaces threshold/observability limits (U1-U8) without overstating resolution. Action quality is strong: A1 (diagnose root cause) and A3 (preserve staged-exposure/flag architecture) directly target the strongest supported mechanisms without weakening protective controls, matching the preferred action, while A2, A4-A6 add reasonable secondary leverage. No harmful, irrelevant, or protective-control-eroding actions are present.
